scope.frame: the harmonic level surfaces of B1846's harmonic time, read by their own conformal modulus
scope.object: m004 (LR) around its whole circle; the excursion member L^6 R L R at s = 1/4, 1/2 and, as a limit, at its tube s = 0
scope.hypotheses: data-free; the modulus from three Dirichlet energies (det E = 1 as the check); two meshing methods; tau reduced to the standard fundamental domain

claim_one_line: THE LEVEL SURFACE'S OWN MODULUS (P-727; data-free): an instrument reading the conformal modulus of a harmonic level surface from its 3D shape and its fibre group alone -- validated on a Fuchsian control of known tau (recovered to < 2e-4 after Richardson; second order; a curved 3D-inverted copy agrees) -- gives the metric's own, fourth reading of the fibre's shape. On m004 the loop is forced at its symmetric levels (s = 0, 1/2: -1/2 + 1.12438i; s = 1/4, 3/4: i) and closes; it sits 0.57% above the golden Teichmuller apex 1/2 + (sqrt5/2)i. On the excursion member L^6RLR: the anti-apex s = 1/2 reads 1/2 + 1.5904i (Re 1/2 forced), 16% above the Teichmuller anti-apex 1/2 + sqrt(15/8) i; s = 1/4 reads -0.3722 + 1.0085i by two independent meshings. The tube level: the surface folds there (a helicoid about the core, which lies on a face of the fundamental domain), and at s = 0 exactly the meshers degenerate; read as the limit of tau(s) by the full group's Ford-domain mesher (controls pass at s = 1/4 and 1/2; the level is regular, |d theta| = 0.042 on the core): Im tau(Sigma_0) = 6.15 +- 0.15 (S306g), far above all three record readings at the tube (apex 3.65, pleated 2.87, tetrahedron 2.58); Re tau not resolved there. 0 of 19.
